title: Go (Genesis 12:1–9)
hookLine: at seventy-five, Abram is told to leave for a land he'll be shown
last: NO NEED TO MAKE A NAME.

lines: GENESIS ZOOMS IN ON ONE MAN.
cards: Seventy-five. By then, the furniture is where it is, the friends are the friends, the doctor knows your name.
Abram is seventy-five, living in a city called Haran, with his wife Sarai, his nephew Lot, and everything they own. Sarai, the text has already said, cannot have children.
Up to now, Genesis has moved fast, whole generations in a verse. Now it slows down and zooms in on one old man, because God is about to speak to him, and the story turns on what he does next.

teach.b: Here's how it begins in the King James Bible: "Now the LORD had said unto Abram, Get thee out of thy country, and from thy kindred, and from thy father's house, unto a land that I will shew thee."

In Hebrew, the first words are lekh lekha: go, and a little extra word that can mean for yourself, or even to yourself. Some Jewish teachers read it as a journey outward that is also a journey inward.
Notice the order of what he has to leave.
Country, then relatives, then his father's house. Each one closer, each one harder. And notice what's missing: the destination.
A land that I will show you.
No map, no name. Then the promise, and remember Babel. The people of Babel said, let us make us a name.
Here God says to Abram: I will make thy name great; and thou shalt be a blessing.

teach.h: WHAT BABEL GRABBED, ABRAM IS GIVEN.
teach.b: What they tried to grab, Abram is given. And not just for himself: in thee shall all families of the earth be blessed. The blessing is meant to spill over.
Then one plain sentence: "So Abram departed." And "Abram was seventy and five years old when he departed out of Haran." He goes.
Along the way, he builds altars. Much later, the letter to the Hebrews sums it up: he went out, not knowing whither he went. Jews and Muslims honor Abraham too, as a father in faith.
And Christians often call him that: the one who went, before he knew where.

how: Christian tradition calls Abraham a father of faith, and his call to go is read at some commissioning services, when people are sent out to new work, a new place or a mission.

o: return home to the city where you were born
stay put and wait for a clear sign
leave for a land not yet named: lekh lekha

games.q: what's inside the call — tap the pairs.

s: God tells Abram exactly where he is going
"unto a land that I will shew thee." no map, no name.
"Abram was seventy and five years old when he departed out of Haran."
the blessing promised to Abram is only for his family
"in thee shall all families of the earth be blessed."

games.q: you're seventy-five and settled. God says: leave your country, your kin, your father's house, for a land I'll show you. what do you do?
o: ask for the name of the land first.
send your nephew to check it out.
games.why: "so Abram departed." Hebrews says he went out, "not knowing whither he went."

practice: Think of something you've been waiting to start until you can see the whole way through, a conversation, an application, a first visit somewhere new, and notice how much you want the map first.
Then ask a smaller question: what is just the first step? If you pray, you can ask for courage for that one step.

wordCard.voice: Go. Lekh lekha in Hebrew. The word that sends Abram, at seventy-five, out of his country toward a land he'll be shown.

orig.note: Hebrew: go, for yourself. The first words of God's call to Abram, and the name of this portion of Genesis in Jewish reading.

carryVoice: Your line: go, not knowing. Abram didn't have the map either, at seventy-five. Until tomorrow.

sources.q: Now the LORD had said unto Abram, Get thee out of thy country, and from thy kindred, and from thy father's house, unto a land that I will shew thee
Abram was seventy and five years old when he departed out of Haran.
